nodes.label: Role Plus Individual Grants
nodes.rationale: Access is a role (the usual path) plus an optional extra_permissions bitmask layered on top, 'for one-off cases where creating a whole new role would be overkill'. Avoids role proliferation at the cost of two places to look when auditing a user's access; the users list flags it with a '+ individual grants' marker. is_admin short-circuits everything - admins always hold every permission.

nodes.label: Last-Admin And Self-Delete Guard
nodes.rationale: The Delete control is withheld when the row is the current user, or when the target is an admin and admin_count <= 1, so the instance cannot be locked out of its own administration. Roles apply the mirror rule: built-in (is_system) roles and roles with users still attached cannot be deleted. UI-level guard only - the POST endpoints must repeat the check.

nodes.label: Monetisable Library Mix Meter
nodes.rationale: Splits ready-to-publish stock into monetisable vs royalty-free segments against a configured monetizable_target ratio, because royalty-free clips gather views but do not earn revenue share - the mix, not the raw count, is the health signal.

nodes.label: Live Queue DOM Contract
nodes.rationale: A container id 'queue-live' plus per-row 'data-job-id' and per-cell 'data-job-status' / 'data-job-percent' hooks form the contract the static poller (app/static/js/app.js) uses to patch job rows in place from /api/queue. Progressive enhancement: the server renders the correct state first, JS only refreshes it.

nodes.label: System Health Panel
nodes.rationale: Renders a list of {level, title, detail} checks with a colour dot. Commented as 'the panel that explains why nothing is happening' - it exists so an idle bot (no connected account, scheduler not running, no rights confirmed) reports its own cause instead of silently doing nothing.

nodes.label: Cross-Platform Statistics Rollup
nodes.rationale: totals.by_platform keys the breakdown by platform name rather than by account, so the same page works as an 'all social medias' view when more adapters than YouTube are connected; channel-level rows are keyed separately by account_id against a channel_stats map.

nodes.label: Status-Keyed Job Actions
nodes.rationale: Job status partitions the row's behaviour: pending/retrying get Cancel and a live-poll data-job-id hook, failed/cancelled get Retry, succeeded/running get neither. The same status vocabulary ('pending', 'running', 'retrying', 'succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled') is repeated in the badge colour ternary and in the dashboard's queue card.

nodes.label: Dependency-Free CSS Bar Chart
nodes.rationale: Views-over-time is drawn as plain CSS div bars whose height is a percentage of the series peak ('plain CSS bars, no charting library'). Trades interactivity and axis labelling for zero JS dependencies, no CDN asset, and a chart that renders identically in the server-rendered page with no client bootstrap.

nodes.label: Publishing Readiness Gate
nodes.rationale: One call to video.blocking_reasons() drives both the banner ('Not publishable yet' with the reason list) and the Publish card, which refuses to render the queue form while any problem stands. Single source of truth for publishability - commented as 'the single most useful thing on this page' - so the UI can never offer an upload the server would reject.

nodes.label: Trend-As-Subject, Never Re-Upload
nodes.rationale: A trend records only the topic and its keywords - the bot never downloads or re-posts source footage. Justified three ways in the UI copy: re-uploading someone else's video is copyright infringement, is demoted as reused content, and cannot be monetised. The reference_url on the detail page is explicitly for human viewing ('watch the example and decide what to make'), not ingestion.

nodes.label: Views-Per-Hour Trend Ranking
nodes.rationale: Trends are ranked by views per hour rather than raw view count, so a fast-rising new topic outranks an old video that accumulated views slowly. The 0-100 score doubles as the progress-bar width; raw views and views_per_hour are surfaced underneath from trend.signals for sanity-checking the score.

nodes.label: Rights And Monetisation Gate
nodes.rationale: Licence type, source, reference and attribution are collected up front and drive a three-way outcome: owned/licensed material can earn, royalty-free gathers views but is excluded from revenue share, and footage whose rights cannot be stated is blocked from publishing outright - 'what gets a channel struck and demonetised'. Rights are a first-class field rather than an afterthought precisely so the block is enforceable.

nodes.label: Inline Shorts Re-Encode
nodes.rationale: A Short must be vertical and under three minutes, so anything else is re-encoded to 1080x1920 with ffmpeg during form submission ('keep the tab open') instead of being deferred to the worker - the operator gets an immediate verdict on the file. The media file is deliberately not replaceable on edit (delete and re-upload instead), so the edit form drops video_file and shows read-only file properties.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Settings Form
nodes.rationale: Instead of a WTForms field per setting, the template loops over grouped specs and switches on spec.kind (bool / choice / time_list / int / float / fallback text) to pick the input widget, reading the current value out of a values[spec.key] map. Adding a setting means adding one spec server-side; the template never changes.

nodes.label: Env vs Database Settings Boundary
nodes.rationale: Deliberate split: secrets and paths (API keys, database URL, media directory) stay in the server .env and need a restart, while operational tuning lives in the database and takes effect on the next background cycle with no restart. Keeps credentials out of the web UI and out of any user's reach.

nodes.label: Accounts Page
nodes.rationale: Lists connected PlatformAccounts with status badge, truncated last_error and token expiry, and offers Test / Connect-Reconnect / Enable-Disable / Disconnect-Delete. Every mutating action is a POST form carrying action_form.hidden_tag() for CSRF, and destructive ones carry data-confirm. Disconnect (drop tokens) is offered while connected and Delete (drop the record) only when not, so tokens are always cleared before a record can vanish. Tokens themselves are never rendered.

nodes.label: Local Backup Procedure
nodes.rationale: Two things cannot be recreated: .env (because of ENCRYPTION_KEY) and the database. A date-stamped copy of both into C:\Users\tolia\SocialBotBackup is the whole backup.

nodes.label: Background Automation Jobs
nodes.rationale: Four recurring APScheduler jobs: upload_queue (5 min), collect_statistics (3 h), research_trends (6 h), maintenance (daily 03:30 UTC). Every job is also runnable on demand from the dashboard 'Run now' or from the command line via flask run-job, so there is a single code path with two triggers.

nodes.label: The Request Path
nodes.rationale: browser to nginx (TLS termination, HTTP->HTTPS redirect, static files, upload limits) to gunicorn (3 workers) to create_app(); then before_request force HTTPS and password change, Flask-Login session to current_user, @permission_required bitmask check, thin blueprint view, after_request security headers.

nodes.label: Flask CLI Command Reference
nodes.rationale: init-db, create-admin, reset-password, list-users, run-job, check, db upgrade. Run from the install directory with FLASK_APP=wsgi.py set.

nodes.label: Development and CI Dependencies
nodes.rationale: pytest and pytest-cov only, layered on top of the runtime set via '-r requirements.txt' so the test environment is the production environment plus a runner - never a different dependency graph.

nodes.label: Runtime Dependency Set
nodes.rationale: Grouped by purpose with a comment per package: the Flask ecosystem for the web tier, APScheduler for background automation, the four google-* packages for the YouTube Data and Analytics APIs, cryptography for Fernet token encryption and python-dotenv for .env, the platform-conditional WSGI servers, and requests.

nodes.label: Redirect URI Display Panel
nodes.rationale: The Platform integrations card prints each adapter's exact redirect_uri as copyable code alongside its configured/hint health state, precisely because a character-level mismatch is by far the most common reason a connection fails - it removes the need for the operator to reconstruct the URI from PUBLIC_BASE_URL by hand. It also surfaces the adapter's supports_trends / supports_revenue capability flags.

nodes.label: Backups and the ENCRYPTION_KEY
nodes.rationale: Three things cannot be regenerated: .env (especially ENCRYPTION_KEY), the database, and the media files. deploy/backup.sh covers config plus database, --with-media covers everything, and it is meant to run nightly from cron. Losing ENCRYPTION_KEY makes every stored OAuth token unreadable and forces every channel to be reconnected by hand, so it must be backed up somewhere other than the server itself.

nodes.label: Append-Only Statistics Snapshots
nodes.rationale: Each collection appends a StatSnapshot instead of overwriting a counter. That costs a little disk and buys the growth curve, 'views in the last 7 days', and an audit of when a number changed. Data API metrics are always available; Analytics API metrics are best-effort because a brand new channel has no analytics rows and that must not stop view counts being recorded. The maintenance job prunes anything over 400 days old.

nodes.label: Platform Adapter Plugin Architecture
nodes.rationale: The platform layer is a registry of adapters implementing PlatformAdapter (app/platforms/base.py) so adding Instagram Reels or TikTok is a new folder under app/platforms/, not a rewrite. Adapters return shared dataclasses rather than raw API responses, which keeps the queue, statistics, dashboard, accounts page and permission model platform-neutral; tests/test_platforms.py enforces the contract.

nodes.label: Thin Views over a Service Layer
nodes.norm_label: thin views over a service layer
nodes.rationale: Views are deliberately thin - they parse the request, call one service and render. Anything that decides something lives in app/services/, which is what lets the scheduler reuse the exact same code paths as the website ('one queue, one code path, two triggers').

nodes.label: Fernet OAuth Token Encryption at Rest
nodes.norm_label: fernet oauth token encryption at rest
nodes.rationale: OAuth tokens are encrypted with Fernet (app/security/crypto.py) before they touch the database and are never rendered in a page. ENCRYPTION_KEY is the only way to read them, so it must be backed up with the database; losing it means reconnecting every channel by hand.

nodes.label: Bounded Version Pinning Policy
nodes.rationale: Every dependency carries both a '>=' lower bound so security patches are picked up on rebuild and a '<' upper bound so a major release cannot silently break a running server. Neither exact pins nor open ranges would give both properties.

nodes.label: Synchronous Manual Job Trigger
nodes.rationale: The scheduler normally runs in a separate 'socialbot-worker' service, so the web process often has no scheduler_jobs to list. Manual buttons run each job inline in the POST request instead - accepted as a slow request ('the page may take a few seconds - an upload run transfers the file before it returns') so the operation is still driveable from a web-only deployment.

nodes.label: Connect an Account Form
nodes.rationale: Collects only platform, display name and is_default, then hands off to the platform consent screen - the form never asks for a token. A notice warns up front that submitting redirects to Google and names the three permissions that will be requested (upload videos, read channel data, read analytics).

nodes.label: Sign-In Page
nodes.rationale: Fills base.html's anonymous_content block so it renders outside the sidebar chrome, includes the flashes partial itself (the signed-in layout would otherwise never show login errors), and points a locked-out operator at the server-side 'flask reset-password <username>' escape hatch rather than offering a self-service reset.

nodes.label: My Account Page
nodes.rationale: Shows the signed-in user's details plus the resolved permission_labels as a keyword cloud, with a special note when is_admin is set because the bitmask list would otherwise understate an administrator's actual access. Records last_login_at and last_login_ip so a user can spot an unexpected sign-in.

nodes.label: Base Layout Template
nodes.rationale: Sidebar navigation plus content column, with two mutually exclusive blocks: 'content' for signed-in pages inside the chrome and 'anonymous_content' for signed-out pages such as login. Ships a data-URI SVG favicon and links only local CSS/JS, consistent with the no-CDN CSP.

nodes.label: Error Page Template
nodes.rationale: Serves 403/404/413/500 from a single template. The body is factored into a local macro and emitted into BOTH the content and anonymous_content blocks, because an error can be raised whether or not a session exists and base.html picks exactly one of those blocks based on current_user.is_authenticated.

nodes.label: render_field Macro
nodes.rationale: One macro renders any WTForms field with its label, help text and validation errors, branching on field.type for BooleanField (checkbox with the label wrapping the help text) and MultiCheckboxField (permission list) so that every form in the site gets identical markup and error presentation for free.

nodes.label: Flash Messages Partial
nodes.rationale: Renders get_flashed_messages(with_categories=true) and maps each category onto a .flash-* colour class, whitelisting success/danger/warning/info and falling back to info so an unexpected category can never emit an unstyled or attacker-chosen class name.

nodes.label: Upgrade Procedure
nodes.rationale: Back up first, stop both services, git pull (which keeps .env, data/ and media/), update dependencies, run flask db upgrade and flask seed-roles, restart and run flask check. seed-roles refreshes the built-in roles so permissions added in a new version reach Administrator and Editor; custom roles are deliberately left alone so an upgrade never silently widens an operator-defined role.

nodes.label: Permission-Aware Navigation
nodes.rationale: Every nav link is wrapped in a current_user.can(Permission.X) check, and whole nav groups are hidden when the user holds none of their permissions, so a user only sees the parts of the site they can open. The view decorators enforce the same rules server-side - hiding a link is convenience, not security. Sign-out is a POST form carrying a csrf_token, matching the 'state-changing actions are POST-only, including sign-out' rule.

nodes.label: Bitmask Permission and Role Model
nodes.rationale: Twelve permission bits stored as one integer. A Role carries a bitmask (Administrator, Editor, Analyst seeded); a User points at one role and may hold extra permissions on top so a one-off grant does not need a whole new role. is_admin short-circuits every check so 'admin should have every access' holds even for permissions added in a future version. Guard rails prevent removing your own admin flag, disabling your own account, or demoting the last administrator.

nodes.label: Security Hardening Notes
nodes.rationale: Werkzeug password hashing with an eight-failure 15-minute lockout and identical messages for wrong password and unknown user (no account enumeration); CSRF on every form with state-changing actions POST-only including sign-out; HTTP-only SameSite=Lax sessions, Secure when TLS is on; CSP, HSTS, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy. The CSP can be strict because the interface ships its own CSS and JS with no CDN, which also means it works on a server with no outbound internet access. ?next= is validated as a same-site path so the login form cannot bounce somebody off-site. Production refuses to start with a missing or placeholder SECRET_KEY or ENCRYPTION_KEY.

nodes.label: Broken python on PATH (Microsoft Store Stub)
nodes.norm_label: broken python on path (microsoft store stub)
nodes.rationale: Typing bare python reaches the Microsoft Store stub, which prints 'Python was not found' instead of running Python. The real interpreter is fine, just not first on PATH, so every command in the guide uses .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe and .\.venv\Scripts\flask.exe explicitly.

nodes.label: PowerShell 5.1 Syntax Constraints
nodes.rationale: The shell here is Windows PowerShell 5.1, where &&, || and ?: do not exist. Commands chain with ; and conditional execution uses if ($?) { }.

nodes.label: .env Machine Configuration
nodes.rationale: Two kinds of configuration are kept deliberately apart. .env belongs to the machine - secrets, paths, ports - and needs a restart to take effect.

nodes.label: Settings Page Operational Configuration
nodes.rationale: The Settings page belongs to the operation, not the machine: editable in the browser and applied on the next background cycle with no restart - automatic publishing, uploads per day, publishing slots, minimum spacing, monetisable ratio, rights confirmation requirement, #Shorts and attribution handling, default privacy and category, trend region, conversion style.

nodes.label: Data Folder Outside OneDrive
nodes.rationale: The project lives inside a synced OneDrive folder. If the bot stored videos there, OneDrive would try to upload every clip to the cloud and could lock the database file mid-write. DATA_ROOT, MEDIA_ROOT and LOG_ROOT therefore point at C:\Users\tolia\SocialBotData, inside the user profile but outside the synced tree.

nodes.label: .env Byte-Order-Mark Hazard
nodes.rationale: The .env file is generated with [System.IO.File]::WriteAllLines rather than Set-Content -Encoding utf8, because the latter prepends a byte-order mark that makes the first key parse as \ufeffAPP_ENV and be silently ignored. Bytes 239 187 191 at the head of the file are the tell; Notepad's plain 'UTF-8' save option adds one too. SQLAlchemy database URLs use forward slashes even on Windows.

nodes.label: Loopback-Only Binding (HOST=127.0.0.1)
nodes.rationale: Binding to the loopback address means the site is reachable from this PC and nowhere else, so no firewall rule is needed and nobody on the network or the internet can reach it. Changing HOST to 0.0.0.0 to reach it from a phone is explicitly refused as advice because it would expose a login page over unencrypted HTTP to the whole network - real remote access means deploying properly with HTTPS. APP_ENV stays production locally because development mode would expose an interactive Python console to anything that reaches the port; FORCE_HTTPS=0 because there is no certificate on localhost.

nodes.label: The Money Rule (Monetisable Running Mix)
nodes.rationale: The PRD requires the majority of published videos to be able to make money. content_service implements this as a running mix over the last 20 automatic uploads rather than a fixed rotation, because a fixed rotation cannot self-correct. If the preferred licence class is empty it falls back to the other rather than waste a publishing slot - the ratio self-corrects on the next pick. Owned or commercially licensed counts as monetisable; royalty-free is publishable view-bait; unverified is never published.

nodes.label: ffmpeg Install on Windows
nodes.rationale: winget install Gyan.FFmpeg, then a NEW PowerShell window - the installer changes PATH and an already-open window will not see it, which is almost always the cause of 'ffmpeg still not found'. If it is genuinely off PATH, set FFMPEG_BINARY and FFPROBE_BINARY to full paths. Excluding the media folder from Windows Defender real-time scanning noticeably speeds up conversion, since ffmpeg is CPU-bound.

nodes.label: YouTube API Daily Quota
nodes.rationale: 10,000 units per day per project, ~1,600 units per upload, so roughly six uploads per day regardless of how many channels are connected. Reading statistics costs 1 unit per call covering up to 50 videos, so collection and trend research are effectively free. The quota resets at midnight Pacific time and the bot marks the job retryable rather than failed, so it resumes automatically with no operator action. More headroom means a quota increase or a separate Google Cloud project per channel.

nodes.label: Rights Confirmation Step
nodes.rationale: Ticking the confirmation box moves a video from draft to ready and into the pool the automation draws from. The confirming username and timestamp are written to the audit log deliberately: approving publication is the moment somebody takes responsibility for the copyright position. Rights-unverified material is blocked from publishing entirely.

nodes.label: Content Rights Policy
nodes.rationale: Refusing unverified material is not caution for its own sake - it is what makes the 'make money' goal achievable. YouTube's Partner Programme rejects channels built on reused content, so re-uploading someone else's video is the fastest route to denied monetisation, copyright strikes and channel termination. Hence trend research collects topics to film, not files to repost; every video records provenance and licence; a named reviewer confirms rights and that confirmation is written to the audit log; royalty-free attribution lines are appended to the description automatically as CC-BY and most stock licences require.

nodes.label: Publish Gate (Video.blocking_reasons)
nodes.rationale: The gate is deliberately evaluated twice - once when the job is queued and again immediately before the transfer - so approval withdrawn while a job sat in the queue still stops the upload.

nodes.label: Shorts Formatting Pipeline
nodes.rationale: YouTube decides whether an upload is a Short by inspecting the file (vertical, at most three minutes), not by an API flag, so video_processing.py must do the real work before upload: probe() honours rotation metadata so a phone video is measured as it will actually play, shorts_problems() reports disqualifiers in plain language, and convert_to_shorts() re-encodes to 1080x1920 H.264+AAC with +faststart in blur, crop or pad style.

nodes.label: View-Velocity Trend Ranking
nodes.rationale: youtube/trends.py ranks the mostPopular chart by views divided by hours since publication rather than raw views, because a three-day-old video with 400k views says more about what is rising now than a two-month-old one with 2M. Scores are normalised to 0-100 so separate runs are comparable. Only the topic and its keywords are kept, never the file, to avoid reused content.

nodes.label: Retryable vs Permanent Upload Failure
nodes.rationale: process_due_jobs() classifies failures: retryable errors back off 5/15/45/135 minutes and try again (this is what makes a quota exhaustion self-healing), while permanent errors mark the job failed and flag the account so a human looks at it.

nodes.label: First Run: Connect, Add, Publish
nodes.rationale: Sign in and change the password, connect the channel via Accounts -> Connect an account and confirm with Test, review the settings defaults, add a video with its rights fields set, confirm rights, then let the worker publish automatically within five minutes of the next slot or force it with the dashboard's 'Plan and run uploads'. Publishing times are UTC, not local.

nodes.label: localhost OAuth Redirect URI
nodes.rationale: Google allows plain http for localhost, so http://localhost:8000/accounts/oauth/callback/youtube works without a certificate. It must say localhost and not 127.0.0.1, because that is what PUBLIC_BASE_URL says. Changing the port means updating four things: PORT and PUBLIC_BASE_URL in .env, the --listen argument in the scheduled task, and the redirect URI in Google Cloud.

nodes.label: OAuth Testing Mode 7-Day Token Expiry
nodes.rationale: While the OAuth consent screen sits in 'Testing' mode only listed test users may authorise the app and their refresh tokens expire after 7 days, which presents as a connection that works and then silently breaks a week later. Clicking 'Publish app' fixes it; for a personal bot using only these scopes Google's verification is usually not required, so the 'unverified app' warning can be clicked through via Advanced -> Go to ... (unsafe).

nodes.label: Test Server Setup
nodes.rationale: For evaluating on a laptop or internal VM with no domain and no certificate: FORCE_HTTPS=0 and BEHIND_PROXY=0 because there is no TLS and no proxy, and SCHEDULER_ENABLED=1 because a single process can safely own the schedule. Google refuses plain http redirect URIs for public hosts but does allow http://localhost, which is what makes the full connect flow testable locally. ENCRYPTION_KEY must still be a real Fernet key - it cannot be faked. Setting Default privacy to private or unlisted exercises the whole pipeline without anything appearing on the channel.

nodes.label: YouTube API Credentials Setup
nodes.rationale: Two APIs must be enabled: YouTube Data API v3 for uploading, metadata, public statistics and trends, and YouTube Analytics API for watch time, subscribers gained and estimated revenue - without the second, uploads still work but statistics show only public counters. The OAuth client must be type 'Web application', not 'Desktop app', because the bot receives the callback in a browser. Consent-screen scopes can be left empty since the application requests its scopes at runtime.

nodes.label: UTC Publishing Times and Timezone Conversion
nodes.norm_label: utc publishing times and timezone conversion
nodes.rationale: Publishing slots are stored and entered in UTC, never local time. On a Pacific-time PC the 09:00/15:00/20:00 defaults land at 02:00/08:00/13:00 local, so the first slot would fire at 2 a.m. when the machine is probably asleep and nothing would publish. Convert with UTC = local + 7 hours in PDT or + 8 in PST, and re-check after the clocks change in March and November.

nodes.label: redirect_uri_mismatch (Error 400)
nodes.rationale: The single most common setup failure. The URI registered in Google Cloud must match PUBLIC_BASE_URL + /accounts/oauth/callback/youtube character for character: https vs http, no trailing slash, same host (www. counts as different), matching port. Because it is so easy to get subtly wrong, the application's own Accounts page displays the exact string to paste.

nodes.label: render_pagination Macro
nodes.rationale: Jinja macros do not accept **kwargs, so extra query-string values (filters, search terms) are passed as a single 'args' dict and merged into every page link - that is what keeps a filtered list filtered when you turn the page. Renders nothing at all when there is only one page.

nodes.label: flask check Configuration Diagnostic
nodes.rationale: The designated first move for any problem - it covers most install failures and prints the fix underneath each failure. It is also the last step the Ubuntu installer runs.

nodes.label: Local Windows PC Guide
nodes.rationale: A ten-step guide written against one specific install (this Windows 11 machine, Python 3.13.2, existing .venv) rather than generically, so every path and command can be pasted verbatim. The PC has to be awake - nothing publishes while it is asleep or shut down, and uploads resume within about five minutes of waking.

nodes.label: Troubleshooting Reference
nodes.rationale: Organised by symptom across installation/start-up, web interface, connecting a channel, uploads, video processing, statistics, trends, TLS and performance - deliberately covering 'the problems people actually hit' rather than an exhaustive error list.

nodes.label: Let's Encrypt TLS with certbot
nodes.rationale: certbot --nginx --redirect is what adds the HTTP->HTTPS redirect the PRD asks for; certbot rewrites the nginx site file in place. Certificates last 90 days and certbot.timer renews at 30 days remaining. The DNS A record must already point at the server before installing, because Let's Encrypt verifies ownership over port 80. The ACME challenge location must stay reachable over plain HTTP or renewal fails.

nodes.label: Moving to PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: Worth it above a few thousand videos or when concurrent writers are needed. Switch DATABASE_URL to postgresql+psycopg and re-run init-db - note that init-db creates an empty schema and does not migrate existing SQLite data, which needs a tool such as pgloader.

nodes.label: SQLite URL Slash Convention
nodes.rationale: sqlite:///relative/path is relative while sqlite:////absolute/path is absolute - an absolute DATABASE_URL takes four slashes. Getting this wrong surfaces as sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file.

nodes.label: Ubuntu Automatic Install
nodes.rationale: deploy/install_ubuntu.sh --domain --email performs eleven steps in order: packages, socialbot system user, directory layout, virtualenv, .env with fresh SECRET_KEY and ENCRYPTION_KEY locked to mode 600, init-db plus a random administrator password, both systemd units, nginx, Let's Encrypt with HTTP->HTTPS redirect, ufw, and finally flask check. The generated admin password is printed once and stored nowhere.

nodes.label: Ubuntu Manual Install
nodes.rationale: Offered for people who want to understand each step or whose environment the installer does not fit - a different init system, a shared host, an existing nginx setup. The shipped systemd and nginx templates contain @PLACEHOLDER@ tokens that must be substituted.

nodes.label: Dedicated System User with No Login Shell
nodes.norm_label: dedicated system user with no login shell
nodes.rationale: A dedicated system user with no shell means that if the web application is ever compromised, the attacker lands on an account that cannot log in and can only write to three directories (data/, media/, logs/) - enforced further by the systemd ReadWritePaths= line.

nodes.label: Windows Task Scheduler Background Task
nodes.rationale: A 'SocialMediaBot' scheduled task runs waitress-serve at logon and restarts it on crash. -LogonType S4U is what suppresses the console window (and is why the registration block needs an Administrator prompt), -ExecutionTimeLimit 0 stops Windows killing a task meant to run forever, -RestartCount 3 recovers from crashes, -AllowStartIfOnBatteries keeps it alive unplugged, and -MultipleInstances IgnoreNew prevents a second copy. LastTaskResult 267009 means running; 0 means it exited. Without -Principal it still works but leaves a console window that must not be closed.

nodes.label: Windows Server Setup
nodes.rationale: Windows has no gunicorn, so waitress-serve runs the web tier and NSSM registers SocialBotWeb and SocialBotWorker as services (exactly one worker instance, for the same reason as the systemd split). The application does not terminate TLS itself, so either IIS with URL Rewrite plus ARR or nginx for Windows fronts it; the proxy must forward HTTP_X_FORWARDED_PROTO=https with BEHIND_PROXY=1 or the app redirects in a loop. Antivirus real-time scanning of media\ noticeably slows ffmpeg.

nodes.label: Single-Process Local Deployment
nodes.rationale: On a server the web tier and the scheduler are split so that several web workers cannot each run the schedule; on one PC a single waitress process with SCHEDULER_ENABLED=1 does both, which is simpler and means one background task is enough. The 'Scheduler started' line on startup is the confirmation that the automation is running inside the web process.

nodes.label: Two systemd Services (Web and Worker)
nodes.rationale: gunicorn runs three worker processes. If each of them started the scheduler, three copies would plan the same upload and the video would be published three times. The web service therefore runs with SCHEDULER_ENABLED=0, and worker.py - a single process - owns the schedule.

nodes.label: Web/Worker Scheduler Split
nodes.rationale: The web service runs with SCHEDULER_ENABLED=0 and worker.py with 1. With three gunicorn workers each running its own APScheduler instance, the same video would be planned and published three times.

nodes.label: Platform-Conditional WSGI Server
nodes.rationale: gunicorn is installed only when platform_system != "Windows" and waitress only when it is, so one requirements file serves both deployment targets without a Windows install failing on a POSIX-only package.

nodes.label: System Actor In Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Audit entries carry a nullable username; a null actor is rendered as 'system' so background-worker actions (scheduled uploads, stats collection, trend research) sit in the same chronological trail as human actions instead of in a separate log. ip_address is likewise optional and blank for worker entries.

nodes.label: Attributed Rights Confirmation
nodes.rationale: Rights confirmation is a named human attestation, not a flag: rights_confirmed_by and rights_confirmed_at are displayed on the ready banner and the form warns 'your name is recorded in the audit log against this confirmation'. Makes the copyright decision personally accountable, and requires PUBLISH_VIDEOS rather than mere MANAGE_VIDEOS.
